reporting-org.narrative: European Commission - Directorate-General for International Partnerships

description.narrative: The overall objective of this action is to build the resilience of women-owned and women-led micro, small, and medium-sized businesses (W-MSMEs) by equipping financial institutions with the knowledge, tools, and capacity to design and deliver gender-responsive financial and non-financial services that reduce vulnerability mostly to climate shocks, but also health and economic shocks.  To achieve this, the action will support 10 to 12 existing EIB clients in Sub-Saharan Africa, including banks, microfinance institutions, and fintechs, to strengthen their ability to offer tailored financial and non-financial solutions that directly address women entrepreneurs¿ resilience needs. This, in turn, will enhance W-MSMEs¿ capacity to manage risks, absorb shocks, and adapt to change. This Action is fully in line with the approach of the flagship Team Europe Initiative - Investing in Young Business in Africa (TEI IYBA). The TEI seeks to facilitate the conditions in which early-stage businesses and entrepreneurs in Sub-Saharan Africa can thrive ¿ especially women and young people. In addition to IYBA-labelled EFSD+ guarantees, the action will specifically complement two IYBA programmes: IYBA Women Entrepreneurship for Africa (WE4A), which focuses on women¿s entrepreneurship, and IYBA SEED, which aims to strengthen local entrepreneurship ecosystems. In light of Africa¿s vulnerability to climate change, the proposed action will support the regional Team Europe Initiative (TEI) on Climate change Adaptation and Resilience in Africa, in particular its pillar 3 `Enhance access to climate adaptation finance for all¿. The Specific Objectives of this action are to: SO 1: Strengthen the capacity of financial institutions to deliver resilience solutions SO 2: Improved women entrepreneurs¿ resilience and agency SO 3: Generate, document, and disseminate evidence on resilience approaches for women entrepreneurs
